class_name: 伝聞-未確認-トノコト類

provenance.pipeline: satsuki v1 (v1.0.1 editorial re-edit: usage-note reshaping corpus-wide, lane discrimination for same-surface families, against prompts/style.md)

patterns.usage_note: Passes on something heard: a plain-form sentence takes って and stops there, the following と言っている dropped, so 明日は休みだって means 休みだそうだ. The sibling lane hangs って on a following noun instead, to name it or to state what it contains (田中って人, 帰るって話). Before this sentence-final って a noun or na-adjective normally keeps だ (雨だって, 学生だって), and it is rare in edited prose outside dialogue.

examples.ruby: 体育館[たいいくかん]の裏[うら]に田中[たなか]さんの財布[さいふ]が落[お]ちているって。
examples.english: Tanaka's wallet is lying behind the gym, apparently.

examples.ruby: 隣[となり]の家[いえ]の犬[いぬ]、夜中[よなか]ずっと吠[ほ]えるって。
examples.english: The dog next door barks all night long, apparently.

examples.ruby: あの映画[えいが]、後半[こうはん]がすごく怖[こわ]いって。
examples.english: They say the back half of that movie is seriously scary.

patterns.usage_note: Relays a message from a specific, identifiable source, especially in business email and phone notes (火曜まで待ってくれるとのことです). It presents the report as received fact and pairs naturally with a named source (〜さんによると), where the siblings って and だって stay casual and are out of place in correspondence. A noun predicate may drop だ before it (来月中旬とのことです).

examples.ruby: 先方[せんぽう]は来週[らいしゅう]の火曜[かよう]まで待[ま]ってくれるとのことです。
examples.english: I'm told the client will hold off until Tuesday of next week.

examples.ruby: 病院[びょういん]から、検査[けんさ]の結果[けっか]は木曜[もくよう]に出[で]るとのことでした。
examples.english: The hospital says the test results will be back on Thursday.

examples.ruby: 工事[こうじ]の完了[かんりょう]は来月[らいげつ]中旬[ちゅうじゅん]とのことです。
examples.english: The work is due to be finished in the middle of next month, I'm told.

patterns.usage_note: Passes on news the speaker has heard, sentence-final and on a falling tone (臨時休業だって); ですって is the polite variant. Three siblings share the string: the same form on a rising tone is a checking question that asks the hearer to confirm (校庭だって？), 'even' on a bare noun (子供だって), and 'even if' on a ta-stem verb (呼んだって). Before a verb or i-adjective speakers usually insert ん first (転勤するんだって).

examples.ruby: あの店[みせ]、今日[きょう]は臨時[りんじ]休業[きゅうぎょう]だって。
examples.english: That place is closed for the day, apparently.

examples.ruby: 田中[たなか]さんのところの赤[あか]ちゃん、女[おんな]の子[こ]だって。
examples.english: The Tanakas' new baby is a girl, apparently.

examples.ruby: 上[うえ]の階[かい]の奥[おく]さん、お花[はな]の先生[せんせい]ですって。
examples.english: The lady upstairs is a flower-arranging teacher, they say.
